Construct a geo-point data request

Source: R/request.R
geo_point_request.Rd

Build a request for environmental or agricultural-economics data at a single geographic point. The request is the input half of the constellation's C6 geo_point_series contract; pass it to collect_point().

Usage

geo_point_request(
  lon,
  lat,
  start = NULL,
  end = NULL,
  variables = NULL,
  source,
  sovereign = FALSE,
  coarsen = NULL
)

Arguments

lon, lat

Numeric scalars. Longitude and latitude in WGS84 decimal degrees (EPSG:4326). lon in [-180, 180], lat in [-90, 90].

start, end

Character scalars (ISO-8601 "YYYY-MM-DD") or NULL. The inclusive date range. Ignored by static layers (for example soil or elevation).

variables

Character vector of source-native variable names, or NULL to let the adapter choose sensible defaults.

source

Character scalar. The id of one registered source adapter (see list_sources()).

sovereign

Logical scalar. When TRUE, the point is treated as sensitive (a sovereign-data coordinate – a grower's paddock, a trial site) and coarsening is applied by default so the exact GPS never leaves the host (see coarsen). Defaults to FALSE.

coarsen

Coordinate-coarsening policy applied to lon/lat before any upstream call, so the exact coordinate is never transmitted. One of: NULL (no coarsening; the default for a non-sovereign point); a single positive number giving the rounding precision in degrees (for example 0.01 rounds to roughly a 1 km cell); or a list(grid = <size>) snapping each coordinate to the nearest multiple of <size> degrees. For a sovereign = TRUE point with coarsen = NULL, a default precision of 0.01 degrees is applied automatically. The request records both the raw-requested coordinate and the coarsened-sent coordinate.

Value

An object of class geo_point_request. When coarsening is applied, lon/lat hold the coarsened coordinate (what is sent upstream) and lon_raw/lat_raw hold the exact requested coordinate (kept on the host for provenance); coarsen_policy records the policy as a string.

See also

collect_point(), list_sources()

Examples

geo_point_request(138.6, -34.92, "2020-01-01", "2020-01-31",
                  variables = c("T2M", "PRECTOTCORR"), source = "nasapower")
#> <geo_point_request> source "nasapower"
#> point: (138.6, -34.92) range: 2020-01-01 .. 2020-01-31
#> variables: T2M, PRECTOTCORR

# A sovereign point: the exact GPS is coarsened to ~1 km before any call.
geo_point_request(138.63124, -34.92871, "2020-01-01", "2020-01-31",
                  source = "nasapower", sovereign = TRUE)
#> <geo_point_request> source "nasapower"
#> point: (138.63, -34.93) range: 2020-01-01 .. 2020-01-31
#> variables: (adapter default)
#> coarsened (sovereign): raw (138.63124, -34.92871) -> sent (138.63, -34.93)
#> policy "precision=0.01"
